specification: Implement exact unit conversion as the package units, consisting of three editable modules (units/fmt.py, units/registry.py, units/convert.py) plus an empty units/__init__.py that must not be edited. Numeric results are fractions.Fraction values equal to the exact mathematical result. units/fmt.py defines to_fraction(value), quantize(x, places) and format_decimal(x, places). to_fraction accepts a built-in int (bool excluded), an instance of fractions.Fraction (subclasses included), or a decimal string consisting of an optional sign, one or more digits, and optionally a dot followed by one or more digits (no spaces, no exponent, no other forms); it returns the exact Fraction value, so '1.609344' is exactly 1609344/1000000. Any other type raises TypeError, and a str that does not have the described form raises ValueError. quantize(x, places), where x is a built-in int that is not a bool, or an instance of fractions.Fraction (subclasses included; any other type, floats and strs included, raises TypeError), and places is an int that is not a bool and is at least 0 (TypeError for a wrong type, ValueError for a negative value), checks x before places and returns the Fraction nearest to x that has at most places decimal digits, with exact ties rounded away from zero (so 5/2 rounds to 3 and -5/2 to -3 at 0 places, and 1/8 rounds to 13/100 at 2 places). format_decimal(x, places) returns the quantized value as a plain string with exactly places digits after the decimal point and no point at all when places is 0; it has at least one digit before the point, a '-' sign appears only if the quantized value is below zero (a value that rounds to zero is printed without a sign), and there are no thousands separators. format_decimal checks its arguments in the same way and in the same order. units/registry.py defines class Registry, which starts empty. base(name, dimension) defines a base unit whose factor is 1; name and dimension must be nonempty strs (TypeError for a wrong type, ValueError when empty; check name before dimension, type before value for each), and a name that is already defined raises ValueError. define(name, ratio, of) defines a unit that equals ratio units of the existing unit of; the new unit has the same dimension as of and its factor is ratio times the factor of of. Checks run in this order: name (nonempty str, as above); ratio through to_fraction (its TypeError or ValueError), then ratio must be greater than zero (ValueError); of must be a str (TypeError) and an already defined unit (KeyError); finally a name that is already defined raises ValueError. A call that raises registers nothing. factor(name) returns the unit's Fraction factor and dimension(name) its dimension string; both raise TypeError for a non-str name and KeyError for an undefined one. names() returns the unit names in the order they were defined. units/convert.py defines convert(registry, value, src, dst) and convert_steps(registry, value, units, places). convert returns the exact Fraction value * factor(src) / factor(dst). Checks run in this order: value through to_fraction (its TypeError or ValueError); src (a str, else TypeError; defined in the registry, else ValueError); dst (the same two checks); then both units must have the same dimension, else ValueError. An undefined unit must surface as ValueError, not KeyError. convert_steps converts value along the sequence of units: units must be a list or tuple (TypeError) holding at least two items (ValueError), and places must satisfy the rules of quantize. Checks run in this order: value through to_fraction, the type of units, the length of units, places (type, then value), and then the conversions are performed one adjacent pair after another, the first failing conversion raising what convert would raise. The conversion from units[i] to units[i+1] is applied to the running amount, and the result of every conversion, including the last, is quantized to places decimal places before it is used as the input of the next one; the starting value itself is not quantized. convert_steps returns the final quantized Fraction. Exception messages are not specified.
